html:
This phase turns everything you practiced into a passing score on the Salesforce Certified Business Analyst (CBA) exam. It covers the exact exam format, the six blueprint areas with their weights, a question-bank methodology, a six-week study schedule, and the exam-taking techniques that protect your score on test day. The roadmap's quiz engine — Training_Question__c, the Training_Question_Scoring flow, and CertificationPrepService.cls — is your daily practice tool.

The facts in this guide were correct at the time of writing, but exam rules and blueprint weights are reviewed and rebalanced by Salesforce over time. Candidates must always re-check the live official exam guide at https://trailhead.salesforce.com before registering.

Learning Objectives

  • State the exact CBA exam format and rules, ...
  • Learn the six blueprint knowledge areas and their weights, ...
  • Build and use a personal question bank, ...
  • Plan a 4–6 week study schedule, ...
  • Apply exam-taking techniques — flag, skip, re-check, ...
  • Allocate study time proportional to blueprint weight, ...

1. The CBA Exam Facts — Know Them Cold

The Salesforce Certified Business Analyst (CBA) exam is a timed, proctored multiple-choice test. The facts below come from the official exam guide and are mirrored as metadata in the org:

FactValue
Scored questions60 (multiple-choice and multiple-select)
Unscored questionsUp to 5 (sprinkled in, not counted)
Duration105 minutes
Passing score72%
Registration feeUS$200 + tax
Retake feeUS$100 + tax
PrerequisiteNone (experience recommended)

In the org, the custom metadata record Certification_Setting__mdt named Business_Analyst holds exactly these numbers so the quiz engine reports them authoritatively:

apex
// Certification_Setting__mdt stores the official facts as metadata.
Certification_Setting__mdt cba = new Certification_Setting__mdt(
  Exam_Code__c        = 'CBA',
  Question_Count__c   = 60,
  Duration_Minutes__c = 105,
  Passing_Score__c    = 72,
  Cost_USD__c         = 200,
  Retake_Cost_USD__c  = 100
);

Two facts get fumbled under pressure: 72% means you can afford roughly 17 wrong of 60 before you fail, and the up-to-5 unscored questions are indistinguishable from scored ones — treat every question as scored.

2. Registering, Retaking, and Re-Checking the Official Guide

Registration happens through the Salesforce certification pages on trailhead.salesforce.com. You pay US$200 plus applicable tax at booking, and it stays yours for that attempt; a failed attempt costs US$100 plus tax to retake. Plan the retake budget before you need it, and never let a failed attempt stop the momentum — the second attempt is the norm, not the exception.

Three pre-booking actions protect your money:

  1. Re-check the live official exam guide for the current weights, question count, duration, and fee. Blueprints are rebalanced, so the numbers in this guide and in Certification_Setting__mdt must always be compared against the live source.
  2. Check your nearest testing option: in-person proctoring at a test center or online proctoring, both with strict identification and environment rules.
  3. Book deliberately — a calm slot after your highest-consistency study week beats the nearest available slot every time.

NOTE: Exam details and blueprint weights change. Always verify the current official guide at https://trailhead.salesforce.com before registering or budgeting a retake.

3. The Six Blueprint Areas

The exam blueprint divides the test into six knowledge areas. Their weights tell you where the score actually lives:

Knowledge areaWeightWhere this roadmap covers it
Customer Discovery17%Phases 2–4
Collaboration and Communication with Stakeholders23%Phases 2, 7, 13
Business Process Mapping12%Phase 3
Requirements Elicitation and Documentation18%Phases 4–6
User Story Creation18%Phase 6
Development Support and User Acceptance Testing12%Phases 9–12

Collaboration is the heaviest area — which is why this roadmap hammers engagement, ceremonies, and change management. In raw questions: roughly 14 land in collaboration, 11 in requirements, 11 in stories, 10 in discovery, 7 in process mapping, and 7 in dev support and UAT.

4. Allocating Study Time by Weight

Study hours should mirror the blueprint, not your comfort zone — studying what you enjoy and skipping what you dread will cost you questions. Allocate like this:

Week(s)Blueprint focusRoadmap materials
1–2Customer Discovery + CollaborationPhases 1–4, 7, 13 guides
3–4Process Mapping + Requirements + StoriesPhases 3–6 guides
5Dev Support + UAT + Gap + ChangePhases 9–13 guides
6Full practice exams + weak-area drilldownPhase 14 quiz engine + MP10

Attack the highest-weight areas second, not last: 23% collaboration can carry a weak area elsewhere. Track drilldown scores per area — Training_Question__c carries a category field for this — and let data pick week six's targets.

5. Building Your Personal Question Bank

Active recall beats re-reading. Writing your own questions forces you to understand the material well enough to mislead yourself on purpose. The academy's bank lives on Training_Question__c — question, options, correct answer, blueprint area, rationale.

MP10 (Cert Drill) in the Phase 15 guide is exactly this: 20 of your own questions across the six areas, a rationale per answer, first-pass score tracked. Rules that make the bank valuable:

  • Spread the 20 questions across all six areas in proportion to the weights.
  • Write one rationale sentence for the correct choice and one for the most tempting wrong choice.
  • Mark any question you get wrong for a deliberate re-study session, not just a correction.
  • Translate real academy scenarios (BrightLogistics, StudyBuddy) into exam-style stems — they train the same "read the behavior, not the buzzword" muscle.

6. The Quiz Engine: Training_Question__c and the Scoring Flow

Practice is a daily habit, measurable in the org: Training_Question__c holds the bank, the Training_Question_Scoring flow records every result into a running first-pass score, and CertificationPrepService.cls reads the pass threshold, count, and duration from Certification_Setting__mdt so mocks mimic the real parameters.

apex
// CertificationPrepService drives quiz mode from the same metadata
// the real exam guide declares, so mocks match the real parameters.
Integer scored   = Integer.valueOf(cba.Question_Count__c);
Integer minutes  = Integer.valueOf(cba.Duration_Minutes__c);
Integer passLine = Integer.valueOf(cba.Passing_Score__c);

Target 10–15 questions daily — small enough to keep, large enough to compound. Timed sets of 20 from week three, a full-length mock (60 questions, 105 minutes) in week six. Always re-read the rationale before retrying a question — option-memorizing inflates score and confidence equally.

7. The Six-Week Study Schedule

Compressed into a table, the recommended rhythm looks like this:

WeekDaily activityWeekly milestone
110 questions + re-read Phases 1–2Blueprint self-audit; weak areas named
210 questions + re-read Phases 3–4Stakeholder + discovery drillcomplete
310–15 questions + Phases 5–6Timed 20-question set
410–15 questions + Phases 7–9Timed 20-question set; rationale review
515 questions + Phases 10–13Full-length timed mock #1
615 questions, weak-area drilldownFull-length timed mock #2 + book exam

Protect the two mocks — they are the only practice that reproduces the real constraint: 105 minutes feel different when real. Between them, drill the lowest first-pass area, found via your Training_Question__c categories.

8. Question Types: Single and Multiple Select

The exam uses two question shapes, and they demand different discipline:

  • Multiple-choice has one correct choice. Read the stem twice, eliminate two distractors you can prove wrong, then choose among the survivors.
  • Multiple-select asks for two or more correct choices, often worded "choose TWO" or "Choose THREE." Every wrong choice costs you the question — there is no partial credit for a half-correct answer.

Multiple-select is where prepared candidates lose points — over-selection. When the stem says "choose TWO," stop at two; the classic failure is the correct answer plus one "plausible" distractor. Read each option as pass/fail against the scenario; a memorized fact that does not apply is a wrong choice.

9. Exam Technique: Flag, Skip, Re-Check

The 105-minute timer is real, and the technique that protects you is a strict loop:

  1. First pass, easy questions first. Do not stop to agonize. If a question does not resolve itself in 60–90 seconds, flag it and move on.
  2. Then the flagged set. The second pass on a hard question after easy wins is measurably clearer — your brain has had minutes of other context.
  3. Eliminate before you choose. Cross out two provably wrong options on every question before deciding; on multiple-select, only count options that survive the scenario test.
  4. Re-check before you submit. The final five minutes review only flagged or uncertain questions, not the ones you answered cold.
  5. Leave nothing blank. An unanswered question is a guaranteed wrong question; a flagged and guessed question keeps a chance.

Pace math: 1.75 minutes per question. Hold the first pass to 45–50 minutes and the flagged pass to 40, and you bank re-check time. Three minutes a question in pass one is how candidates finish two-thirds of the test.

10. Reading Scenario Questions for Behavior

Most CBA questions are short scenarios, and they are graded on the behavior you pick, not the buzzwords you recognize. Read every scenario with three filters:

  1. The actor — who is doing the work? A discovery interviewer, a project manager, a UAT coordinator, an admin. The correct answer almost always matches the actor's role.
  2. The action — what concrete step is the scenario testing? Capture the requirement, route the lead, log the defect, write the note. Name it in your own words before reading the options.
  3. The acceptance criterion — what would prove the step done? The exam nearly always rewards the configured, simplest fit that satisfies the criterion; elaborate and over-engineered answers exist as distractors.

A BrightLogistics-flavored example: "A dispatcher reports that web leads still sit in a shared inbox. The BA notices the assignment rule has no routing criteria. What should the BA do first?" The actor is a BA, the action is diagnosing adoption, and the accepted answer is to inspect the routing configuration and confirm the to-be flow — new-feature, retraining, and rebuild options are wrong-order.

The same filters apply to the academy's own scenarios: BrightLogistics for the full SDLC, StudyBuddy for data-modeling and story questions. If you have practiced deciding "what's the simplest configured fit" on those two worlds, the exam's unfamiliar company names will not matter.

11. The Week Before, the Day Of, and After

Protect the final hours — the plan does not end the night before:

The week before:

  • Book the exam and the day of free; no new material after Wednesday — review rationale sheets and weak-area drills only.
  • Re-read the official guide one final time to confirm the current weights, durations, and fees.
  • Prepare identification (photo ID) and, for online proctoring, clear your desk and room per the proctor rules.

The day of:

  • Sleep, eat, arrive early; the exam room is colder and the clock faster than the office.
  • Re-check the timer discipline from section 9 before you start the test.
  • On multiple-select questions, read "choose TWO" twice.

After:

  • If you pass, file the score and start your certification portfolio (Exercise 9.1) and elevator pitch (Exercise 9.2) in Phase 15.
  • If you do not pass, the report shows per-area performance. Book the retake (US$100 + tax), drill exactly the weak areas, and go again — the second attempt is the plan, not a failure.

12. Certification as a Career Catalyst

The CBA credential is industry proof of exactly what this roadmap exercises: discovery, collaboration, mapping, requirements, stories, UAT. It does not replace the portfolio — it accredits it. The strongest candidates carry both: a certificate that proves the discipline and a portfolio (Exercises 9.1, 9.2) that proves the work.

Keep three habits after you pass: re-verify the blueprint periodically, keep growing your Training_Question__c bank, and treat every career scenario as exam practice — "we need a portal" still gets the disciplined fit-gap response the exam rewards.

Hands-On Exercises

1. Build Your 20-Question CBA Bank

Create the MP10 cert-drill bank with the engine in mind.

Steps:

  1. Write 20 questions distributed across the six blueprint areas by weight.
  2. Give each question four options, a correct answer, and a rationale for correct and tempting-wrong choices.
  3. Set the blueprint-area category on each Training_Question__c record.

Expected result: 20 questions that map to the blueprint and can be scored by the Training_Question_Scoring flow.

What it proves: that writing questions is the strongest active-recall study method on the roadmap.

2. Run a Timed 20-Question Set

Simulate real pacing at exam intensity.

Steps:

  1. Set 35 minutes and a quiet environment (20 questions × ~1.7 min).
  2. Apply flag, skip, re-check on this set.
  3. Score first-pass, then review the rationale for every mistake.

Expected result: a measured first-pass score with the weak areas named.

What it proves: that technique practice matters as much as content practice.

3. Blueprint Self-Audit

Map your current readiness to the six areas.

Steps:

  1. Rate yourself 1–5 per blueprint area from your drill scores.
  2. Order the areas by gap between weight and score.
  3. Write the week-five and week-six drill plan targeting the biggest gaps.

Expected result: a ranked study to-do list proportional to where you lose points.

What it proves: that study time should follow the blueprint weights, not your comfort.

4. Decode Five Scenario Questions

Practice actor / action / acceptance reading.

Steps:

  1. Take five scenario questions (from your bank or the guides).
  2. Underline the actor, the action, and the acceptance criterion in each stem.
  3. Explain in one sentence why the simplest configured answer wins each.

Expected result: five stems decoded with behavior-first reasoning.

What it proves: that the exam rewards configured, simplest fits — the exact philosophy of this roadmap.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
CBASalesforce Certified Business Analyst — the exam this roadmap targets
BlueprintThe official breakdown of exam knowledge areas and weights
Scored questionA question that counts toward the 60-question score
Unscored questionAn experimental question, up to 5, that does not count
Passing scoreThe 72% threshold equating to roughly 43+ correct of 60
Multiple-selectA question requiring two or more correct choices, no partial credit
Registration feeUS$200 plus tax paid at booking
Retake feeUS$100 plus tax for a failed attempt
Certification_Setting__mdtCustom metadata record Business_Analyst storing the exam facts
Training_Question__cThe question bank object storing questions, options, answers, and area
Training_Question_ScoringThe flow that evaluates answers and records first-pass scores
CertificationPrepServiceThe Apex service driving quiz mode from certification metadata
Flag, skip, re-checkThe time-management loop for the 105-minute test
Analog watch testPrefer question-skip over blank answers — every question carries a chance

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can state the CBA exam facts from memory: 60 scored, up to 5 unscored, 105 minutes, 72% pass, $200 + tax, $100 retake.
  • I can recite the six blueprint areas and all six weights.
  • I know the largest-weight area is Collaboration and Communication (23%).
  • I have built a personal question bank covering all six areas.
  • I run timed practice under the ~1.7-minutes-per-question rule.
  • I apply flag, skip, re-check on every timed set.
  • I decode scenario questions by actor, action, and acceptance criterion.
  • I have re-checked the live official guide at trailhead.salesforce.com before booking.
  • I have completed MP10 (Cert Drill) and assembled evidence for Exercises 9.1 and 9.2 in Phase 15.

Summary

You learned the exact CBA exam facts — the fees, the duration, the 72% pass line, and the up-to-5 unscored questions — and the six blueprint areas with their weights, with Collaboration and Communication at 23% leading your study time. You built a personal question bank on Training_Question__c, scored it through the Training_Question_Scoring flow and CertificationPrepService.cls, and scheduled a six-week plan with two full-length mocks and weak-area drilldown. The flag, skip, re-check technique and the actor-action-acceptance reading pattern are now reflexes you can carry into the proctored room. Remember to re-verify the live official guide at https://trailhead.salesforce.com before you book — and then go earn the credential your Phase 15 portfolio is ready to back up.
